proof_summary: Take \(n=18\): since \(\sigma(18)=39\), its reduced denominator is \(18/\gcd(18,39)=6\), while \(\sigma(6)=12\) makes the reduced denominator at \(6\) equal to \(1=2^0\). Thus the denominator at \(18\) has the required property, but \(18\) itself does not, because its denominator \(6\) is not a power of two (it is neither \(1\) nor \(2\), and every higher power is divisible by \(4\)).
